title: Data2Agent dataset manifest
description: What a dataset IS. Contains no timestamps, no absolute paths and no host details, so that repeated ingests of identical bytes produce byte-identical manifests. Run-specific facts belong in provenance.json.

dataset_id.description: SHA-256 fold over the sorted (path, file checksum) pairs.

missing_value_convention.description: How token-valued absences were resolved. Governs how every missing count below should be read.

layout_declaration.description: The layout declaration supplied at ingest (--layout), identified by the SHA-256 of its bytes, or null when none was. Part of the manifest because it governs how the tables were read: a re-ingest under another declaration is another manifest, so a relationships sidecar bound to the old one is refused. The file's name is run-specific and lives in provenance.configuration.layout_declaration.

metadata_candidates.description: Files a metadata recogniser applied to and could not finish reading. An open question, never a finding: a candidate is not metadata, and an empty metadata_files beside a non-empty list here means 'nothing was recognised, and these were never examined'.

relationships.description: An empty array means relationships were NOT determined, never that the dataset has none.

borisProjectSummary.description: Present only on a file detected as a BORIS project. Counts, never contents: no subject, behaviour or observation name is copied. null means the section is absent or not a collection, which is not the same as zero.

path.description: POSIX-style, relative to the dataset root.

detected_by.description: How the format was established. 'container' means the archive's own member list identified it, e.g. OOXML part paths inside a ZIP. 'content' means the parsed content confirmed or overruled the extension's claim, e.g. a '.boris' name over JSON with BORIS's project keys.

extension_format.description: What the file's extension claimed, recorded separately from what the bytes showed. Present only when the extension matched a known format.

extension_conflict.description: True when the extension's claim contradicts the observed content. The extension is never rewritten; both statements are kept.

fileEntry.description: One regular file, as bytes on disk. Symlinks are never inventoried: they are listed in 'skipped' and raised as a warning, because following one would put bytes from outside the dataset boundary into a manifest that claims to describe it.

header_row.description: First header row: the 1-based spreadsheet row, or for a delimited file the physical line on which the header record starts. Null when the table has no non-blank row.

header_rows.description: How many rows the header spans; above 1 only when declared.

data_starts_row.description: Row (or line) where observations begin; row readers start here, and source_row stays the file's own row or line number.

header_source.description: 'first-non-empty': the first non-blank row, the pre-D2A-97 behaviour; 'detected': a later row chosen by the rule after skipping preamble; 'declared': stated by the layout declaration.

header_cells.description: Only for a multi-row header: this column's cells in the header block, top row first, as written -- before any forward fill of an upper label. The column's name is the non-blank (filled) parts joined by ' / '.

dtype.description: The shape of the observed tokens. NOT a statement about what the column means. Cells resolved to missing contribute no type.

values.description: Cells holding a value under the active convention. Includes unresolved ambiguous tokens, which are values the file records.

missing.description: missing_empty + missing_sentinel. Read it together with the manifest's missing_value_convention.

missing_sentinel.description: Cells holding a token the active convention resolves to missing.

sentinel_tokens_seen.description: The exact tokens resolved to missing, as written, with counts.

ambiguous_tokens_seen.description: Tokens such as 'unknown' or '-' that no built-in convention resolves. Counted as values, reported for a human to rule on.

distinct_exact.description: False when the value set exceeded the enumeration cap and 'distinct' is only an upper bound.

unique.description: Whether every value in the column differs from every other. Present only for columns whose name is one of the subject-identifier names uniqueness is tracked for; absent means the question was not asked, and null means it was asked and the column exceeded the tracking cap.

metadataFile.description: A file, or one part of a file, recognised as carrying metadata -- by filename convention or by content structure. The claim is structural: that the file follows a metadata convention or has the shape of a metadata record. It is never a claim about what the metadata says.

path.description: The file, or '<workbook path>#<sheet name>' when the metadata is one worksheet of a workbook.

recognised_by.description: Which rule fired. 'content' means the filename matched nothing and the file's structure was recognised instead.

filename_convention.description: What the filename rule said, whichever rule actually fired. Null means no filename convention matched; recognition by content never hides that.

kind.description: 'document': the file's content is the metadata record. 'embedded': metadata carried inside a file that is also dataset payload, such as a registry worksheet. An embedded entry does not remove its file from the data files.

file.description: The dataset file carrying this metadata. Equal to 'path' for a whole file.

basis.description: The observed structure that produced the recognition: the signature that matched, and the columns or keys it matched on. What was seen, not what it means.

metadataCandidate.description: A file a metadata recogniser applied to and could not finish reading. Recorded so that 'we looked and found nothing' stays distinguishable from 'we could not look'.

reason.description: Why the recogniser could not finish: the optional reader for the format is absent, the content could not be profiled, or the document would not parse.

identifier.description: A pattern match in text. NOT a claim that the identifier resolves or is valid.

missingValueConvention.description: A named, declared rule for which cell tokens count as missing. Never inferred per dataset.

id.description: 'declared' when the dataset states its own convention; otherwise a built-in id such as 'default-sentinels'.

source.description: Where the convention came from, in plain words.

ambiguous_tokens_resolved.description: Always false: tokens such as 'unknown' or '-' are reported, never resolved to missing.

workbookSheetProfile.description: Observed properties of one worksheet. Distinct from tableProfile: a sheet has no encoding or delimiter, and carries a sheet locator instead. 'rows' is null when the content could not be read, because no row count was observed.

header_row.description: First header row: the 1-based spreadsheet row, or for a delimited file the physical line on which the header record starts. Null when the table has no non-blank row.

header_rows.description: How many rows the header spans; above 1 only when declared.

data_starts_row.description: Row (or line) where observations begin; row readers start here, and source_row stays the file's own row or line number.

header_source.description: 'first-non-empty': the first non-blank row, the pre-D2A-97 behaviour; 'detected': a later row chosen by the rule after skipping preamble; 'declared': stated by the layout declaration.

reader.description: Which optional parser read the sheet, chosen from the format the bytes established. The parser's version is run-specific and is recorded in provenance.configuration.workbook_readers, never here. 'cell_values: cached' means a formula's last computed value was read, not its expression. Absent from manifests written before D2A-94, all of which were read by openpyxl.

tables.description: Table paths the declaration names; every one matched a profiled table, or ingest refused to run.

headerDetection.description: How the header was chosen. 'rule' names the versioned deterministic rule; 'detected_header_row' is what that rule chose, recorded even when a declaration overrode it; 'confident: false' means the rule could not establish a header and the first non-empty row was used, as before D2A-97. 'skipped_rows' lists every non-blank row before the data that is not a header row, with its row number (the spreadsheet row, or the line a delimited record starts on) and why it was skipped: 'sparse' (fewer than half the header's non-empty cells), 'key-value-label' (first cell is text ending in ':'), or 'declared'.
